14 Silent Mind

We’re moving all courses to the new Self Mastery Community


Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/fG9cRHEdAJI

Silent Mind lesson - 3 audios

Walking and Perception

Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Silent Mind lesson audios. Practice the breathing and
attention exercises in each. You may want to listen multiple times.

2. Rotate through the different ones at different times. The mind likes
variety and this will help avoid boredom.

3. You are practicing different ways to turn off the internal chatter of the
mind. Once your mind is quiet you will perceive yourself and the world
much differently. Emotions, body sensations, other people, colors and movements
all become heightened experiences. Explore all of these as you open your world to new
possibilities.

Some notes

In these practices it is my intention that you be able to shift your attention and quiet
your mind. Effectively turning off all the internal dialog chatter in your head. If this
happens for a few seconds or minutes your perception of other senses can heighten, and
your body becomes more relaxed.

Your experience each time will vary. However, with practice over time, your experiences
and enjoyment of a quiet mind will expand. Your ability to do this is increased with
practice. The part of the brain with all the chatter is the prefrontal cortex. It has all that

                                                                                                                                   1/4

chatter because it is trying to manage fears. When you become relaxed, that part of the
brain is able to turn off, and your brainwaves change from beta to alpha. This is a
calmer feeling in your body. When this happens you experience your self and the world
in new ways.

The is kind of a “bending reality” practice. It is taking a number of elements that you
have been working with and shifting the way you use them consciously. Your Attention,
Emotion, Perspective, and Personal Power. You are focusing on things, or abstract
things like emotion, and using that to change your state. Your nervous system may
relax. That’s the idea.

There are many types of meditation. They accomplish different things. One of them is to
give your mind something positive to do. The mind is not inclined to stay quiet. Even
after you let go of all your beliefs it will continue to create dreams and narrate. Dreams
are what I call those images, words, thoughts, emotions, and virtual worlds of our
imagination. You won’t stop a mind from creating dreams, that is what it does. Just like
you won’t stop a horse from wanting to get up and move around. What you can do is
direct it in a manner that you want to go.

What you can change is what your mind dreams. You can change this by giving it
something positive, kind, loving, entertaining, funny, joyful, grateful, or loving to
imagine, dream about, and tell stories about. Or in the walking perception practice, you
can quiet it just by giving it a way to perceive. You will continue to create emotions for
the rest of your life. The choice you get is to choose what type of emotions. You can
create emotions that cause you to suffer, or emotions based in love. The amount of
personal power and effort is the same.

It might come down to this question, “how do you want to feel?”

Then go practice that.

In these practices you are turning off the frontal neocortex. it is the part of the brain
that makes all that chatter. It is the part of the mind active due to stress. Because we
have beliefs about being rejected, not liked, fears of losing money we are in a low state
of stress. Our mind is looking how to avoid small rejections, and how to be accepted,
liked, and successful. It is always working on that problem until you and your nervous
system feel safe and secure. The breathing practices inform your nervous system and
brain that you are safe and emotionally secure so you can finally rest and turn off that
part of your brain. It may take a while for your mind to get this signal and get really
quiet.

Resistance to change

Since it is a new experience and unfamiliar, your characters may respond with
resistance. They tend to stick with narratives and ideas they know and have repeated.
They avoid anything new. Their words for it will be “weird” or “strange.” In this case,

                                                                                                                                   2/4

“weird” and “strange” are good. You want new experiences. You want to break free from
the stories/narratives of the past, and the emotions they come with.

So, to help, whenever you are engaged in any new experience, notice when your
characters label it with “weird”, “strange”, or other judgmental words. Then counter
that, and replace it with less judgmental words.

Example: “That wasn’t strange. That was just different, and new. New is good. New
possibilities and new experiences are what I want. I don’t want the old stories and
routines.”

You can apply this shift in logic and wording away from resistance labels to words of
curiosity.

At this point we don’t expect you to have mastery over your emotions. If that was the
case, I wouldn’t have put up those other audios programs and tools. You are just getting
your hands on some techniques and are only a couple weeks into practicing some of
them.  After you practice on your belief system and mind for a while you will become
skillful. After you become skillful you will find the deeper stuff to work on.

So watch out for discouragement, expectations of being “done” or wishing it were over
“so you can get on with your life.” Etc. These are sabotaging stories that push you away
from practicing by expecting all the change to just land on your lap because you showed
up.

Change happens because you work on it.

Common questions

What if I can't quiet the mind?
Not surprising. It’s not a straight forward act.  It’s not important, or really the goal to
quiet the mind. It’s more about quieting your Self. In that state when you are quiet, you
might be aware that the mind is very busy with chatter and talking.

The intent is to focus yourself and that you be quiet. In that intent you can heighten
your awareness of yourself as Consciousness separate from your mind. You as
consciousness are going to practice these meditations and being quiet. The mind may
follow right away or it may take some time.

If your mind follows that’s great. If not, that is still success.

I do the meditations but the results are inconsistent ???
Inconsistent is normal. Some days or even at different times of the same day your
response will be different.

You might write out the story of the character that “expects” or “wants” the results to be
consistent. What is the problem with getting different results at different times?

                                                                                                                                   3/4

I’ve never had two meditations be exactly the same with the results or experiences.

Supporting videos


Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/2WW7dAgdzbQ

Self Awareness

Noticing how you notice things changes how and what you notice. In the process you
are doing something different. When you do something different, you become different
and you experience yourself and the world in a new way.

It is an adventure of perception and new experiences.

Your ego will have fear and try to avoid anything new.

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/2GDc42j-dNQ

How being accepting helps you change

Judgment, rejection, criticism, and other reactions can cause you to spend a lot of
energy and not go anywhere bit deeper into a pit. You can exhaust yourself in those
stories. Refrain, and you gather personal power.

Self Mastery 1 Next Steps...

We’re moving all courses to the new Self Mastery Community

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/8SWX-EvV3ro

Summary of practice

1. Listen to the audio About Quitting

2. Go back to what wrote in your journal when you started a few months ago.
Read about the mindset and emotions your past self was in at that time. Reflect on the
changes you have made.

3. Measure your progress and see your growth. Maybe you made some of your
goals. Maybe you didn’t succeed but you are closer. Step outside what the Judge has
to say about “success”. Only ask yourself, “Are you closer to being the person you want
to be?” Then you are succeeding.

4. Decide if you want to stop here, or if you want to make more changes.

Some notes
There are probably going to be lessons that went well. There are probably going to be
exercises that didn’t gel and you struggled with. That’s how progress goes. Overall, I
would expect that, sometimes you you feel good, and sometimes you are struggling.
That would be about right. More on that below.

At this point you can have all sorts of different results.

Some people just listen through the first time. They are so used to the school approach
and intellectual pursuit of knowledge is their automated program. Maybe actively doing
the practices draw too much resistance and so listening is enough.

Even with this, your awareness will have grown, and you will have a lot more
understanding of your mind. The downside is that the Judge will take this new

                                                                                                                                           1/4

information and use it as some kind of image of perfection. It will claim that is how you
should be, and beat you up for not being there yet. So there is an upside and down side
with this effort.

To reiterate, if this is you, then this is progress. You have an evaluation process that
requires that you kick the tires for a while before you buy into doing the exercises part
of the process.

You might be one of the people that didn’t do any writing. You listened, you practiced in
your mind. You watched the characters as best you could and did all of the practices in
your head. That’s progress.

You might be one of the people that wrote a lot, and worked on most of the lessons and
exercises. You might feel like there is a lot more to do. That’s also progress.

No matter what, I would expect that at times you still fall into emotions and stories and
characters. This is to be expected. You should also be better at getting your self out of
those emotional holes.

If you are recall from the Gratitude session on building a new house and dismantling
the old one. At this point I would think that your new house is partially built, and your old
house of emotions and beliefs is still partially standing. You spend time going back and
forth between the two different emotional houses and their respective points of view.

You feel good at time, and you fall into old stories and emotions at times. This is where
I would expect most people to be. You know more about what is possible, and you still
have some old beliefs that pull you back into old emotional patterns.

This is to be expected.

You have just gotten the last of the basics to practice in the last few weeks. It’s all still
very new. You haven’t had enough time to become experts or even proficient at all the
new skills yet. And, then there is part about effectively putting them to work to dismantle
and dissolve the remaining emotions and beliefs.

Because of this learning curve in building new practices, the beginning here is where
change is the slowest. It speeds up from here as you practice.

Resistance to change
One of the resistance tricks that you are going to have to move past is boredom.
Boredom with any skill building practice is a tempting hole to fall into. One of the ways
that your ego will set you up for the “boredom” trap to fall into is that it will say. “Hey,
let’s go back and practice the basic exercises. We should be better at those before we
go on to the more advanced stuff.”

Once the ego has you going back over old material it can throw out the boredom

                                                                                                                                    2/4

temptation trap, “Hey, we have heard this before, and this isn’t new. We aren’t learning
anything. This is getting kind of boring. Let’s go play video games, (or insert any old
distracting behavior here.”

Now it has you not practicing the old stuff, and not working on the new stuff.  It is now
maintaining it’s turf and unconscious control over your attention.

The exercises are intentionally different to help avoid the boredom trap. The Phase II is
also a different set of practices that help you avoid the boredom trap. And, they help
you deepen your understanding, and strengthen your Basic series skills. So you don’t
need to improve your basic series skills before you go on, even if all you did was listen
to the audios and not practice them. The boredom trap still applies.

Common questions

Should I go on to the Self Mastery Course II or to the Relationship course next?
As a default, I suggest Self Mastery Course II next. In some cases, if you have some
relationship issues/beliefs you want to address right away, then the second option is to
do both.

The relationship course does not have a lot of time consuming exercises. A lot of it is
taking the belief hunting processes you learn in the Self Mastery I and II series and
apply them to limiting relationship beliefs.

I feel you can do the Relationship course in parallel with the Self Mastery Course II, or
as you review the Self Mastery I exercises.

Should I go back and practice the Self Mastery I series and get better at them before
Phase II?
I think that what is in Self Mastery Course II will make you much better at the skills in
the First course than just repeating the basics.

Course II takes you into deeper understanding, and helps you apply some of the SM 1
practices better. You will also learn new approaches and skills that are helpful for
dismantling sticky beliefs.

One of the resistance points that people fall into the trap of is “trying to get these
practices perfect.” This keeps you from learning new skills and perspectives that will be
helpful. A more effective approach for change is to work on improving and developing
skills. This doesn’t mean getting them perfect.  If this is your focus you will grow
instead of be trapped in self-judgment about -“not being perfect”.

Supporting videos

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/qlt07d89c8E


                                                                                                                                   3/4

How you see your “self”.

There is a mechanism in the mind that allows it to project an image or an idea of what
you are and then for you to feel like that is you. This is very powerful, but doesn’t give
you an accurate representation of what you are.

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/0mhSnXIWYL0

Who are you really?

When I have people do this exercise there are two important aspects to notice. First is
to see how the mind not only makes multiple false images of you, but how each one
can seem real when you are in that point of view. The other aspect to notice is how you
as consciousness can make your mind do this at will.
